name: Solène Ito-Mwamba
description: Solène Ito-Mwamba is a Tier 4-born feed personality who built her audience by spending 90 days living embedded in the Shelf — documented entirely through unfiltered BCI broadcast — and then spending 90 days in the Spire, broadcasting both with equal unflinching detail. The resulting feed-series, called 'The Distance,' ran in 2222 and became the most-discussed cultural artifact in M88 that year, praised by Shelf residents for its honesty and despised by Tier 5 figures who recognized their own spaces and faces in the footage. She currently occupies an ambiguous cultural position: too honest for corporate comfort, too Tier 4 in origin for full Shelf embrace.
cultural_impact: 'The Distance' forced M88's general public to confront the experiential gap between tiers in visceral, felt terms rather than statistical ones — the BCI format meant audiences didn't just watch, they felt Solène's discomfort, hunger, and shock. Three Tier 4 and 5 figures who appeared in the Spire segment have filed ongoing civil suits, and at least one has attempted to have the feed delisted.
key_figures: Maris Vandenberghe-Olu (Tier 5 socialite currently suing her)
locations: Caldwell Fringe, Tier 1 (her Shelf embedded location)
The Aerie, Tier 5 residential spire (her Spire access point)
Studio Liminal, Tier 3 (her current production base)
story_hooks: Solène is planning a third installment of 'The Distance' — this time embedded with a CorpSec unit for 90 days — and both CorpSec command and Shelf resistance networks are independently trying to get to her before she starts filming, for opposite reasons.

During her Shelf embed, Solène witnessed something she chose not to broadcast — a Tier 1 family hiding something in a sealed apartment — and now that family has disappeared, and someone is reviewing her unbroadcast raw feed files.

A Spire figure from 'The Distance' has offered Solène an enormous sum to produce a 'corrective' feed showing their charitable work — and the offer comes with a subtle threat embedded in the contract language that her legal team has just noticed.
controversy: Maris Vandenberghe-Olu's lawsuit claims Solène's BCI capture of a private Spire dinner constitutes 'emotional trespass' — the legal argument, that broadcasting felt experience of a private space violates privacy in a new legally unprecedented way, is being watched by every BCI platform operator in M88 as a potential landmark case.
